notes: This contract pins the embedded Connection Lost scenario to the exact IEEE 1516.1-2025 C++ FederateAmbassador callback. The callback is invoked on a best-effort basis after the private transport endpoint forces the member out of the execution; the focused selected-file lane proves its distinct §4.4 fault-description record is durable before that callback and writer release. The directive cases validate configured DELETE_OBJECTS, UNCONDITIONALLY_DIVEST_ATTRIBUTES, DELETE_OBJECTS_THEN_DIVEST, CANCEL_PENDING_OWNERSHIP_ACQUISITIONS, and CANCEL_THEN_DELETE_THEN_DIVEST automatic-resign dispositions before that callback, plus the bounded NO_ACTION forced-resign policy that retains the object, divests owned attributes, offers assumptions to a survivor, and emits no automatic removal. The focused TSO-cutoff cases additionally prove the faulted federate's callback alongside a surviving recipient's independently traced ordinary and directed timestamped interaction callbacks, timestamped Reflect Attribute Values callback, and timestamped Remove Object Instance callback; the reflection and deletion paths are independently delivered to two staggered survivors, deletion remains timestamped across an automatic-delete collision, and both a late timestamped reflection and a late directed interaction remain distinct from their later receive-order automatic deletions. Bounded evoked and immediate asynchronous attribute cases prove Reflect Attribute Values, matching Time Advance Grant, then receive-order automatic removal in the same TAR. The composite asynchronous-delivery case also pairs that cutoff with HLAreportFederateLost. It is source/API traceability only; protected review, package support, remote transport, and conformance remain open.
